title: The Summer My Dad Let Go

pre.en: What had Chen's dad done before Chen looked back?
pre.zh: 小陈回头之前，爸爸做了什么？
options: He had let go of the seat.
He had fallen off a bike.

intro: 一篇小故事：小陈现在每个星期六骑车去 Ruth 的陶艺工作室，却怕车站旁的大环岛；回家路上，他想起八岁那年爸爸教他骑车的夏天。读的时候留意 wish + 过去式：说对「现在」的不满和愿望，动词要往回退一步（I wish I were …、I wish you could …）。结尾的一通电话有个小反转。

sentences.en: In October, Tom and I spent far too much on two new bikes.
sentences.zh: 十月份，我和 Tom 买了两辆新自行车，钱花得实在太多了。

sentences.en: The shop knocked twenty pounds off mine because the bell didn't work.
sentences.zh: 因为我那辆车铃不响，店里便宜了 20 英镑。

sentences.en: Now I cycle to Ruth's studio every Saturday, and I love it, apart from one thing: the big roundabout near the station.
sentences.zh: 现在我每个星期六都骑车去 Ruth 的工作室，骑得很开心，只有一件事除外：车站附近那个大环岛。

sentences.en: As soon as I see it, the fear kicks in.
sentences.zh: 我一看到它，心里就开始发怵。

sentences.en: So I make an excuse, usually something about my chain, then get off and walk.
sentences.zh: 于是我就找个借口，一般是说链条有点毛病，然后下车推着走。

sentences.en: Tom says I should take my time, but the drivers behind me don't agree.
sentences.zh: Tom 说我慢慢骑就行，可我后面的司机可不这么想。

sentences.en: He keeps telling me to sign up for a cycling course for adults.
sentences.zh: 他老劝我去报个成人骑车课。

sentences.en: Honestly, I wish I were braver.
sentences.zh: 说真的，我真希望自己胆子大一点。

sentences.en: And I wish the roundabout had traffic lights, or at least fewer buses.
sentences.zh: 要是那个环岛有红绿灯就好了，或者公交车少一点也行。

sentences.en: Last Saturday, on my way home, I remembered the summer of 2004, when I was eight.
sentences.zh: 上周六回家的路上，我想起了 2004 年的那个夏天，那年我八岁。

sentences.en: The day after I'd handed in my last homework of the year, Dad took a small red bike out of the shed.
sentences.zh: 交完那学年最后一份作业的第二天，爸爸从棚子里推出一辆小红车。

sentences.en: My cousin had handed it down to me, along with a helmet that was far too big.
sentences.zh: 那是表哥骑过传给我的，还附送一个大得离谱的头盔。

sentences.en: Every evening after dinner, Dad ran behind me in the car park, holding the seat and shouting, "Keep going!"
sentences.zh: 每天晚饭后，爸爸都在停车场里跟在我后面跑，扶着车座喊：「继续骑！」

sentences.en: I fell off eleven times — I counted.
sentences.zh: 我摔下来十一次——我数过。

sentences.en: I wished I could walk everywhere for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 恨不得这辈子都走路算了。

sentences.en: I lost my balance on every corner, and I learned the hard way that you can't stop a bike with your feet.
sentences.zh: 每到拐弯我就失去平衡，吃了不少苦头才明白：用脚是刹不住自行车的。

sentences.en: Then one evening, I finally plucked up the courage to look back.
sentences.zh: 后来有一天晚上，我终于鼓起勇气回头看了一眼。

sentences.en: Dad was standing in the middle of the car park, ten metres away.
sentences.zh: 爸爸站在停车场中间，离我有十米远。

sentences.en: He'd let go of the seat long before.
sentences.zh: 他早就松开车座了。

sentences.en: On Sunday I rang him and said, "I wish you could cycle with me here."
sentences.zh: 星期天我给他打电话，说：「真希望你能来这儿跟我一起骑车。」

sentences.en: He laughed.
sentences.zh: 他笑了。

sentences.en: "Me? I never learned.
sentences.zh: 「我？我压根就没学会过。

sentences.en: Why do you think I was running?"
sentences.zh: 不然你以为我为什么跟在后面跑？」

cards.note: to take an amount away from a price
英国路口很常见；美式说 traffic circle。
the fear 加 the，指的是「那种熟悉的害怕」；fear of sth 对……的恐惧。
to start to have an effect
to give a reason for something you did or did not do, which is often not the true reason
也是「链子」：a gold chain；连锁店是 a chain of shops。
to do something slowly and carefully without hurrying
cards.tip: your 跟着人称变：take my time；说「在某事上慢慢来」用 take your time over sth。
cards.example: There's no rush — take your time and check everything.

cards.zh: 报名参加；注册（某项服务）
cards.note: to agree to take part in something or to start using a service, usually by giving your details
cards.tip: 后面接名词；也能接 to do：sign up to run a marathon。
cards.example: I've signed up for a Spanish class on Thursday evenings.

cards.zh: 上交；交给（失物招领、老师、前台）
cards.note: to give something to a person in charge, for example something you found or a piece of work
英语不分堂、表、男女、长幼，都叫 cousin。
to give something to a younger person in your family
cards.tip: 传给谁用 to；这样传下来的衣服、东西叫 hand-me-downs。
cards.example: My grandmother handed this ring down to my mother.

cards.note: 骑车戴的叫 bike helmet / cycle helmet；英国法律不强制，但大多数人都戴。
to continue doing something, especially when it is difficult
cards.tip: 鼓励别人时常用；后面也能接 doing：keep going straight on。
cards.example: You're nearly at the top — keep going!

cards.note: to fall from something such as a bike, a horse or a wall
cards.tip: 从什么上掉下来就直接加宾语：fall off a bike；原地摔倒是 fall over。
cards.example: My phone fell off the table and landed in my coffee.

cards.note: to become unable to stay standing or sitting steadily, so that you start to fall
cards.tip: your 跟着人称变：lose my / his balance；反过来「保持平衡」是 keep your balance。
cards.example: She lost her balance on the ice and sat down hard.

cards.zh: 吃了苦头才学会；从教训中学到
cards.note: to learn something by making mistakes or having a bad experience
cards.tip: 后面常跟 that + 句子，说学到了什么；英式过去式也可以写 learnt。
cards.example: I learned the hard way that you should always save your work.

cards.note: to make yourself brave enough to do something that frightens you
cards.tip: 后面接 to do；也可以省掉 the：pluck up courage。
cards.example: It took me a week to pluck up the courage to ask for a pay rise.

cards.note: 英式拼写 metre，美式 meter；ten metres away 是「十米开外」。
to stop holding something or someone
cards.tip: 后面有宾语时用 let go of sth；没有宾语只说 let go：Let go! let 的过去式、过去分词都是 let。
cards.example: Don't let go of my hand in the crowd.
